threats.description: An attacker on the internet tampers with HTTP requests at the TLS-terminating load balancer (request smuggling / header injection) to reach internal portal and API services.
Session or identity spoofing against the patient portal lets the attacker act as a legitimate patient and reach the protected API.
An information-disclosure flaw in the REST API exposes protected health information (PHI) and internal service tokens to an attacker who has pivoted from the portal tier.
Token forgery or SSO bypass against the Keycloak identity provider lets the attacker mint trusted assertions and impersonate clinical staff.
The PostgreSQL patient-records database leaks PII/PHI and payment records to an attacker pivoting from the application tier.
The Memcached session/lookup cache is poisoned to hijack authenticated clinician sessions or alter cached clinical lookups.
HL7 / clinical-event messages on the RabbitMQ broker are tampered with to alter orders, results, or downstream clinical workflows.
A clinician opens a malicious email attachment and the vulnerable mail client is exploited to gain code execution on the back-office workstation.
